facts.statement: Albert Burrer donated the fossils found at the quarry to Professor Eberhard Fraas between 1906 and 1914.
facts.quote: From 1906 until 1914 when the quarry closed, Burrer donated the finds to paleontologist Professor Fraas of the königliche Stuttgarter Naturalienkabinett.

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene described the first specimen of Efraasia in 1907–1908, originally naming it Teratosaurus minor.
facts.quote: A specimen of a basal sauropodomorph, SMNS 11838, was first described by Friedrich von Huene in 1907–1908 and named as a new species of Teratosaurus: T. minor.

facts.statement: Adam Yates published a comprehensive study on Efraasia fossils in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, Adam Yates published a study incorporating these and other fossils from the Late Triassic of Germany.

facts.statement: Efraasia was a herbivore that lived approximately 210 million years ago during the Late Triassic in what is now Germany.
facts.quote: It was a herbivore which lived during the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, around 210 million years ago, in what is now Germany.

facts.statement: Efraasia was a lightly built, medium-sized sauropodomorph measuring about 6 to 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: Efraasia was a lightly built, medium-sized sauropodomorph, about 6 to 7 m long.

facts.statement: Adult Efraasia is estimated to have reached a length of 6.5 meters, with the largest known specimen having a femur length of 627 mm.
facts.quote: Yates in 2003 has estimated the adult length at 6.5 m; the largest specimen is SMNS 12843 with a femur length of 627 mm.

facts.statement: Efraasia had a light build with gracile hands and feet relative to its size.
facts.quote: Efraasia was lightly built for its size, with gracile hands and feet.

facts.statement: Efraasia likely exhibited facultative bipedalism, capable of walking on both two and four legs.
facts.quote: Like many "primitive" sauropodomorphs, Efraasia might have been partially bipedal and partly quadrupedal.

facts.statement: Efraasia possessed long fingers and mobile thumbs adapted for grasping food, while its wrist structure may have facilitated quadrupedal locomotion.
facts.quote: It had long fingers and mobile thumbs, with which it would have been able to grasp food, but the shape of its wrists might have allowed it to walk easily on all fours.

facts.statement: Some researchers debate whether Efraasia was an obligate biped, arguing that its lower arm anatomy prevented pronation and downward-facing hands.
facts.quote: Some researchers however, contend that the lower arm did not allow pronation, a rotation of the radius around the ulna, so that the hand could not be directed downward, making the animal an obligate biped.

facts.statement: Von Huene identified gastroliths associated with specimen SMNS 12667, suggesting Efraasia swallowed stones to aid digestion.
facts.quote: Von Huene identified a cluster of stomach stones (gastroliths) in association to specimen SMNS 12667.

facts.statement: Efraasia possesses two unique autapomorphies: a raised crescent-like ridge on the inner pubis shaft and a vaulted bony web between braincase extensions with a central platform.
facts.quote: Yates identifies two unique derived traits (autapomorphies): the presence of a raised crescent-like ridge on the upper part of the inner side of the pubis shaft; and the presence of a vaulted bony web between two lower extensions of a braincase bone, the processus basipterygoidei, with a raised central bony platform on top of the vault.

facts.statement: In 1965, Charig reclassified Efraasia as a plant-eating sauropodomorph.
facts.quote: Only in 1965, Charig established they were plant-eating sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: Modern phylogenetic analysis places Efraasia as a basal sauropodomorph, more derived than Thecodontosaurus but less derived than Prosauropoda or Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Modern phylogenetic analysis has indicated that Efraasia is a basal sauropodomorph, somewhat more derived than Thecodontosaurus, but less than either the Prosauropoda (including Plateosaurus) or the Sauropoda.

facts.statement: Efraasia minor is the only known species of the extinct genus Efraasia, a prosauropod sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in Europe.
facts.quote: Efraasia minor (de «Eberhard Fraas menor») es la única especie conocida del género extinto Efraasia de dinosaurio sauropodomorfo prosaurópodo, que vivió finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 210 millones de años, durante el Noriense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Efraasia is known from a juvenile specimen, but adults are estimated to have reached 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Conocido por un ejemplar juvenil, se estima que en edad adulta llegó a medir 6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Like other primitive sauropodomorphs, Efraasia likely alternated between quadrupedal and bipedal locomotion.
facts.quote: Como todo los sauropodomorfos primitivos alternaba su marcha entre la posición cuadrúpeda y la bípeda.

facts.statement: Efraasia is considered a primitive sauropodomorph that is more advanced than Thecodontosaurus but less advanced than prosauropods like Plateosaurus or early sauropods like Anchisaurus.
facts.quote: Efrasia es considerado un sauropodomorfo primitivo, pero más avanzado que el Thecodontosaurus con el cual es contemporáneo, pero menos que los prosaurópodos como el Plateosaurus o los saurópodos primitivos como el Anchisaurus.

facts.statement: Efraasia had a slender build for its size, featuring graceful hands and feet.
facts.quote: Efraasia fue ligeramente construida para su tamaño, con manos y pies gráciles.

facts.statement: Efraasia possessed long fingers and mobile thumbs used for grasping food, though its wrist structure might have allowed easy quadrupedal walking.
facts.quote: Tenía dedos largos y pulgares móviles, con los que habría podido agarrar la comida, pero la forma de sus muñecas podría haberle permitido caminar fácilmente a cuatro patas.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Efraasia's lower arm structure prevented pronation, forcing it to be an obligate biped.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, algunos investigadores sostienen que la parte inferior del brazo no permitía la pronación , una rotación del radio alrededor del cúbito , por lo que la mano no podía dirigirse hacia abajo, lo que hacía que el animal fuera un bípedo obligado.

facts.statement: Efraasia had a small, pointed, triangular skull with four teeth in the premaxilla.
facts.quote: El cráneo es pequeño, puntiagudo y triangular. Hay cuatro dientes en el premaxilar.

facts.statement: Efraasia's neck was moderately elongated but slender.
facts.quote: El cuello es solo moderadamente alargado pero delgado.

facts.statement: Efraasia had low neural spines on its tail.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales de la cola son bajas.

facts.statement: Yates identified two unique derived traits in Efraasia: a raised crescent-shaped crest on the inner upper side of the pubis axis, and a domed bony network between lower extensions of the basipterygoid process with a raised central bony platform.
facts.quote: Yates identifica dos rasgos derivados únicos, autapomorfías, la presencia de una cresta en forma de medialuna levantada en la parte superior del lado interno del eje del pubis; y la presencia de una red ósea abovedada entre dos extensiones inferiores de un hueso de la base del cerebro, el proceso basipterygoideo, con una plataforma ósea central elevada en la parte superior de la bóveda.

facts.statement: Von Huene identified a group of stomach stones, gastroliths, associated with specimen SMNS 12667.
facts.quote: Von Huene identificó un grupo de cálculos estomacales, gastrolitos, en asociación con el espécimen SMNS 12667.

facts.statement: Efraasia was found in Germany in the Lowenstein Formation in Baden-Wurttemberg and has undergone four major reclassifications.
facts.quote: Encontrado en Alemania en Formación Lowenstein en Baden-Wurttemberg, a principios del , este dinosaurio ha pasado por 4 grandes reclasificaciones.

facts.statement: Initially, Friedrich von Huene placed Efraasia in the genus Teratosaurus in 1908 because its bones were mixed with a Rauisuchia reptile.
facts.quote: En un principio, debido a que sus huesos se hallaban mezclados con un reptil Rauisuchia fue colocado entre estos bajo el género Teratosaurus por Friedrich von Huene en 1908.

facts.statement: Eberhard Fraas discovered the initial error, retained the name for the jaw, and erected the genus Efraasia.
facts.quote: Eberhard Fraas descubrió el error y conservó el nombre para la mandíbula, y erigió el género Efraasia.

facts.statement: Master mason Albert Burrer began exploiting the Weiße Steinbruch quarry near Pfaffenhofen in Württemberg in 1902.
facts.quote: Albert Burrer, albañil maestro de corte, en Maulbronn, en 1902 comenzó a explotar Weiße Steinbruch, una cantera cerca de Pfaffenhofen en Württemberg.

facts.statement: From 1906 until the quarry closed in 1914, Burrer donated his findings to paleontologist Professor Fraas of the königliche Stuttgarter Naturalienkabinett.
facts.quote: Desde 1906 hasta 1914, cuando la cantera se cerró, Burrer donó los hallazgos al paleontólogo Profesor Fraas del königliche Stuttgarter Naturalienkabinett.

facts.statement: In 1912, Eberhard Fraas reported two partial skeletons, SMNS 12667 and SMNS 12684 collected in 1909, which he assigned to a new species of Thecodontosaurus, T. diagnosticus.
facts.quote: En 1912, Eberhard Fraas informó sobre dos esqueletos parciales, SMNS 12667 y SMNS 12684 recolectados en 1909, que asignó a una nueva especie de Thecodontosaurus, T. diagnosticus.

facts.statement: Peter Galton reassigned Fraas's specimens to the new genus Efraasia in 1973 because Palaeosaurus was a non-diagnostic tooth genus aside from homonymy issues.
facts.quote: Peter Galton reasignó los especímenes de Fraas al nuevo género Efraasia en 1973, porque Palaeosaurus, aparte de los problemas de homonimia, era un género de dientes no diagnósticos.

facts.statement: In 2003, Adam Yates published a study incorporating these and other fossils from the Late Triassic of Germany.
facts.quote: En 2003, Adam Yates publicó un estudio que incorpora estos y otros fósiles del Triásico Superior de Alemania.

facts.statement: Yates chose E. minor as the specific name, providing the new combination Efraasia minor for the type species Teratosaurus minor, making it the only valid species name for the taxon.
facts.quote: Yates eligió E. minor como el nombre específico, proporcionando a la especie tipo Teratosaurus minor la nueva combinación Efraasia minor, que es, por lo tanto, el único nombre de especie válido del taxón.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing stratum was part of the Stubensandstein member of the Lower Löwenstein Formation, dating to the Norian stage.
facts.quote: Este estrato fue parte del miembro Stubensandstein de la formación Löwenstein inferior, que data del Noriano.

facts.statement: Efraasia lived during the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is sometimes recovered as the sister taxon to the last common ancestor of the two largest groups.
facts.quote: El género a veces se recupera como el taxón hermano del último ancestro común de los dos grupos más grandes.

facts.statement: Like many "primitive" sauropodomorphs, Efraasia may have been partially bipedal and partially quadrupedal.
facts.quote: Como muchos sauropodomorfos "primitivos", Efraasia pudo haber sido parcialmente bípedo y en parte cuadrúpedo.

facts.statement: Yates estimated the adult length at 6.5 meters in 2003, with the largest specimen, SMNS 12843, having a femur length of 627 millimeters.
facts.quote: Yates en 2003 ha estimado la longitud del adulto en 6,5 metros, el espécimen más grande es SMNS 12843 con una longitud de fémur de 627 milímetros.

facts.statement: Efraasia was once thought to be a relatively small dinosaur, about 2 to 3 meters long, but this was due to the most complete known fossils being from juvenile animals.
facts.quote: Una vez se pensó que Efraasia era un dinosaurio relativamente pequeño, de aproximadamente 2 a 3 metros de largo, pero esto se debía a que los fósiles más completos que se conocen son de animales juveniles.
